Bacalhau com Natas; Bacalhau à Gomes de Sá), Sardinhas Assadas (fresh Atlantic sardines grilled whole over charcoal, seasoned with coarse sea salt, and eaten over thick slices of rustic sourdough bread with roasted bell peppers), Francesinha (Porto's legendary epic sandwich: thick bread stacked with wet-cured ham, linguiça sausage, fresh sausage, and steak, covered with melted cheese and smothered in a rich beer-tomato sauce, topped with a fried egg and surrounded by fries), Polvo à Lagareiro (tender octopus roasted with smashed garlic, rosemary, and drowned in rich extra virgin olive oil, served with roasted crushed potatoes / batatas a murro), Caldo Verde (comforting green soup of pureed potatoes and onions with finely shredded collard greens and slices of smoked chouriço sausage), Arroz de Marisco (soupy seafood rice brimming with crab, shrimp, clams, and mussels in a fragrant cilantro-tomato broth), Porco à Alentejana (marinated pork cubes cooked with clams, garlic, and coriander), and world-renowned wines: Port Wine (fortified sweet wine from the Douro: Tawny, Ruby, Vintage), crisp effervescent Vinho Verde, and smooth Alentejo reds.), traditional music and dance (Fado (the soul of Portugal - melancholic, deeply emotional urban song accompanied by the 12-string Portuguese guitar / guitarra portuguesa, UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage: legendary 'Queen of Fado' Amália Rodrigues, modern superstars Mariza, Ana Moura, Carminho, Camané); Pimba popular folk dance music; rock/pop icons (Madredeus, The Gift); classical masters (Maria João Pires - world-renowned concert pianist).; Vira (traditional energetic folk dance of the Minho region performed in circle formations with raised arms and fast footwork), Corridinho (fast Algarve partner dance), Chula; modern contemporary dance company Companhia Nacional de Bailado (CNB).), literature (Luís de Camões (Os Lusíadas - 1572 national epic recounting Vasco da Gama's voyage and Portuguese history), Fernando Pessoa (The Book of Disquiet / Livro do Desassossego, master of heteronyms like Alberto Caeiro, Álvaro de Campos, and Ricardo Reis), José Saramago (Nobel Prize in Literature 1998: Blindness / Ensaio sobre a Cegueira, Baltasar and Blimunda), Eça de Queirós (The Maias, The Crime of Father Amaro), Sophia de Mello Breyner Andresen, António Lobo Antunes.), and sports (Football (Futebol - national passion: UEFA Euro 2016 Champions, UEFA Nations League 2019 Champions; Cristiano Ronaldo - 5-time Ballon d'Or winner, all-time leading international goalscorer in men's football history with over 130 goals; Eusébio, Luís Figo - 2000 Ballon d'Or; legendary coach José Mourinho; elite clubs: Benfica, Sporting CP, FC Porto), Surfing (Nazaré - home of the largest surfable waves on Earth, where surfers ride 30-meter Atlantic monster waves off Praia do Norte; Peniche WSL pro stop), Roller Hockey (multiple World and European Champions), Athletics (Nelson Évora - Olympic Triple Jump Gold; Pedro Pichardo - Olympic Gold Tokyo 2020 and Silver Paris 2024), Canoeing (Fernando Pimenta - multi-time Olympic and World Champion).).

name: Romania
nationalDay: December 1 (Great Union Day - Ziua Marii Uniri, commemorating the 1918 unification of Transylvania, Bessarabia, and Bukovina with the Kingdom of Romania)
nationalAnthem: Deșteaptă-te, române! (Awaken Thee, Romanian!)
motto: None (historical: Nihil Sine Deo - Nothing without God)
coastline: 225 km (Black Sea coast, from the Danube Delta to Vama Veche)
highestPoint: Moldoveanu Peak (Vârful Moldoveanu, 2,544 m in the Făgăraș Mountains of the Southern Carpathians)
longestRiver: Danube River (Dunărea - 1,075 km along the Romanian border and territory, forming the spectacular Iron Gates gorge and Danube Delta before emptying into the Black Sea), Mureș River (761 km), Olt River (615 km)
majorLakes: Lake Razelm (Razim - 415 km² Black Sea lagoon complex)
Bâlea Lake (glacial lake in the Făgăraș)
Saint Anne Lake (Lacul Sfânta Ana - only volcanic caldera lake in Romania)
majorMountains: Carpathian Mountains (Southern Carpathians / Transylvanian Alps: Făgăraș, Retezat, Bucegi, Piatra Craiului; Eastern Carpathians; Western / Apuseni Mountains)
climate: Temperate continental climate with four distinct seasons: hot summers with frequent thunderstorms, crisp golden autumns, and cold snowy winters across the mountains; moderated by maritime influences along the Black Sea coast
naturalHazards: High seismic activity centered in the deep Vrancea seismic zone (devastating 1977 earthquake)
Seasonal river flooding along the Danube and Siret valleys
Winter blizzards across the eastern plains (Crivăț wind)
environmentalIssues: Air quality improvements in urban industrial centers
Combating illegal logging in Carpathian virgin forests via digital forestry tracking ('Forest Inspector')
Danube Delta wetland preservation
biodiversity: Europe's premier wilderness sanctuary: home to over 50% of Europe's brown bear population (over 7,500 wild brown bears - largest population in Europe outside Russia), 3,000 grey wolves, and 1,500 Eurasian lynx; the Danube Delta UNESCO Biosphere Reserve is the best preserved delta in Europe, hosting over 300 bird species including Europe's largest colony of white pelicans, pygmy cormorants, and sturgeons
languages: Romanian (official Eastern Romance language, the only Latin-derived language in Eastern Europe)
Hungarian (recognized regional minority spoken by ~6% in Transylvania)
currency: Romanian Leu (RON, lei)
legislature: Parliament of Romania (Parlamentul României: Chamber of Deputies / Camera Deputaților of 330 seats and Senate / Senat of 136 seats)
mainPoliticalParties: Alliance for the Union of Romanians (AUR)
UDMR / RMDSZ (Democratic Alliance of Hungarians in Romania)
latestElections: Simultaneous local and European Parliament elections June 2024; presidential and parliamentary elections late 2024 / early 2025
politicalSituation: Stable democracy navigating dynamic multi-party coalition governance; leading Eastern European pillar of NATO and the EU; achieved landmark accession into the Schengen Area for air and maritime borders on March 31, 2024, with land border integration advancing; massive highway infrastructure expansion underway.
foreignRelations: Member of European Union (joined 2007), NATO (joined 2004), WTO, Council of Europe, OSCE, and BSEC; strategic military and security partnership with the United States (hosting the Aegis Ashore missile defense system at Deveselu and Mihail Kogălniceanu Air Base); accession to the Schengen Area achieved for air and sea travel in March 2024; OECD accession process advancing.
military: Romanian Armed Forces (Armata Română: Land Forces, Air Force, Naval Forces; defense expenditure at 2.5% of GDP, deploying F-16 fighters, Patriot surface-to-air missile batteries, HIMARS rocket artillery, and incoming F-35 stealth jets).
adminDivisions: 41 counties (județe) and 1 municipality (the capital city of Bucharest)
history: Ancient Dacia under King Decebalus flourished until conquered by Roman Emperor Trajan in 106 AD (commemorated on Trajan's Column in Rome). Roman colonization produced a Latin-speaking Daco-Roman population that endured centuries of migrations. In the 14th century, the independent principalities of Wallachia and Moldavia emerged, defending their sovereignty against Ottoman expansion under heroic leaders: Mircea the Elder, Vlad the Impaler (Vlad Țepeș - Prince of Wallachia), and Stephen the Great (Ștefan cel Mare - Prince of Moldavia). Transylvania flourished under Hungarian and Habsburg rule with fortified Saxon towns. In 1859, the unification of Moldavia and Wallachia under Prince Alexandru Ioan Cuza formed modern Romania. King Carol I led Romania to recognized full independence in the 1877–1878 Russo-Turkish War. Romania fought with the Allies in WWI, resulting in the historic Great Union (Marea Unire) of December 1, 1918. Suffered immense tragedy in WWII, losing territories and experiencing the Holocaust and Soviet occupation. The brutal communist dictatorship of Nicolae Ceaușescu was overthrown in the violent Romanian Revolution of December 1989. Modern Romania transformed into a booming high-tech economy, leading IT hub, and stalwart member of NATO and the EU.
recentEvents2020_2026: Officially entered the Schengen Area for air and maritime borders on March 31, 2024, eliminating border passport controls across all international airports and seaports; accelerated construction of the landmark A7 Moldavia Motorway and A1 Sibiu-Pitești Carpathian mountain highway; expanded the strategic Mihail Kogălniceanu Air Base into NATO's largest forward military operating base in Europe; inaugurated the historic Brăila Bridge over the Danube (third-longest suspension bridge in Europe, opened late 2023); advanced offshore natural gas extraction projects in the Black Sea (Neptun Deep by OMV Petrom and Romgaz).
historicalFigures: Trajan (Roman Emperor who incorporated Dacia)
Vlad the Impaler (Vlad Țepeș - Prince of Wallachia, inspiration for Dracula)
Stephen the Great (Ștefan cel Mare - Prince of Moldavia)
Mihai Viteazul (Michael the Brave - first prince to unite Wallachia, Moldavia, and Transylvania in 1600)
King Carol I (first King of modern Romania)
Queen Marie of Romania (beloved diplomat and WWI humanitarian icon)
George Enescu (monumental classical composer and violinist)
Constantin Brâncuși (Father of Modern Sculpture: The Endless Column, Bird in Space)
Henri Coandă (pioneer of aviation and discoverer of the Coandă effect)
Nadia Comăneci (gymnastics legend - first perfect 10 in Olympic history at Montreal 1976)
Mircea Eliade (philosopher and historian of religions)
Eugen Ionescu (Eugène Ionesco - playwright of the Theatre of the Absurd)
Emil Cioran (philosopher)
ethnicGroups: Hungarians (Magyars, predominantly in Transylvania and Szeklerland) ~6.0%
education: University of Bucharest (founded 1864), Babeș-Bolyai University in Cluj-Napoca (UBB - largest university in Romania), Politehnica University of Bucharest, Technical University of Cluj-Napoca, Alexandru Ioan Cuza University in Iași, West University of Timișoara; world-renowned for competitive programming, mathematics olympiad champions, and computer science talent.
healthcare: Universal statutory health insurance through the National Health Insurance House (Casa Națională de Asigurări de Sănătate - CNAS); Floreasca Emergency Hospital and Fundeni Clinical Institute in Bucharest, Cluj-Napoca County Emergency Hospital.
socialCustoms: Mărțișor (giving red-and-white braided silk amulets on March 1 to welcome spring - UNESCO), Colindatul (traditional Christmas caroling performed by men and youth wearing fur hats), Easter candle processions (taking the Holy Light home on Easter Eve), gathering for outdoor grătar (barbecue) with mici and beer on May 1.
etiquette: Warm, expressive, and deeply hospitable; greeting with a firm handshake or double-cheek kiss; bringing flowers (in odd numbers only, reserving even numbers for funerals) or fine wine/sweets when invited to someone's home; removing shoes indoors.
nationalIdentity: Defined by an unbroken Latin linguistic island surrounded by Slavic and Hungarian neighbors, pride in ancient Daco-Roman roots, the mystical beauty of Transylvanian castles and Carpathian forests, rich Orthodox spiritual architecture, and brilliant scientific and mathematical ingenuity.
industries: Automotive manufacturing (Dacia / Renault Group in Mioveni - producing the Dacia Duster and Sandero, Europe's best-selling car; Ford Otosan in Craiova)

Information technology, artificial intelligence, and software development (UiPath - Romania's first $30B+ robotic process automation decacorn; Bitdefender - cybersecurity giant; major R&D centers in Cluj-Napoca, Bucharest, Timișoara, and Iași, termed 'Silicon Valley of Eastern Europe')
Energy engineering, oil refining, and offshore gas (OMV Petrom, Romgaz, Nuclearelectrica)
Aerospace components and defense engineering (Romaero, IAR Brașov)
Chemicals, fertilizers, and plastics (Chimcomplex)
Mechanical engineering and electrical equipment
Food and beverage processing (Ursus, Timișoreana, Borsec mineral water)
agriculture: Cereals (wheat, maize / corn, barley - one of the European Union's top grain exporters)
Sunflowers (#1 sunflower seed producer and exporter in the EU)
Rapeseed and soybeans
Wine viticulture (Dealu Mare, Murfatlar, Cotnari, Târnave - #5 wine producer in the EU)
Fruits (plums for Țuică, apples)
Pork, poultry, and sheep farming (Telemea cheese)
naturalResources: Offshore natural gas reserves (Neptun Deep in the Black Sea - over 100 billion cubic meters)
Crude petroleum reserves (Ploiești historic oil fields)
Arable fertile chernozem soils in the Danubian Plain
Gold, silver, copper, and salt reserves (Praid, Slănic Prahova)
Extensive virgin beech and coniferous forests in the Carpathians
energy: Over 80% carbon-free electricity: Nuclear power (Cernavodă Nuclear Power Plant operating two CANDU reactors, generating ~20% of electricity, with Units 3 & 4 and NuScale SMRs under construction), Hydroelectric power (Iron Gates / Porțile de Fier cascades on the Danube and mountain reservoirs generating ~30%), booming onshore wind (Fântânele-Cogealac 600 MW - one of Europe's largest onshore wind farms) and solar PV.
exports: Motor vehicles, commercial vans, and automotive parts (Dacia Duster, Dacia Sandero, Ford Puma)
Electrical machinery, wiring harnesses, and electronic components
Refined petroleum products and natural gas
IT software and digital enterprise automation services
imports: Machinery, mechanical appliances, and electronic data processors
tourism: Over 14 million visitors enthralled by Transylvania's medieval fairy-tale towns (Brașov, Sibiu, Sighișoara - birthplace of Vlad the Impaler), dramatic Bran Castle ('Dracula's Castle'), Peleș Castle in Sinaia (one of Europe's most stunning Neo-Renaissance royal palaces), the spectacular Transfăgărășan alpine highway, the Painted Monasteries of Bucovina (UNESCO), wooden churches of Maramureș, and wildlife boat expeditions through the Danube Delta.
employment: Surging tech software engineering, automotive design, advanced manufacturing, and modern agriculture; dynamic IT hubs in Cluj-Napoca, Bucharest, Timișoara, and Iași.
debtInflation: Monetary policy directed by the National Bank of Romania (Banca Națională a României - BNR) managing the Romanian Leu; public debt-to-GDP under 52% (well below the EU 60% ceiling).
transport: Transfăgărășan Highway (DN7C crossing the Făgăraș peaks, hailed by Top Gear as 'the best driving road in the world') and Transalpina (DN67C reaching 2,145 m); rapidly expanding motorway network (A1, A2 Sun Motorway to Constanța, A3 Transylvania, A7 Moldavia); Brăila Bridge over the Danube (opened 2023); modern Bucharest Metro; CFR passenger railways.
airports: Henri Coandă International Airport Bucharest (OTP - handling over 15 million passengers annually)
Iași International Airport (IAS - newly opened modern terminal)
Brașov-Ghimbav International Airport (GHV - newly built international airport)
ports: Port of Constanța (largest and deepest seaport on the Black Sea, premier grain export terminal of Europe, and maritime terminal of the Rhine-Main-Danube canal corridor), Port of Galați (river port), Port of Brăila.
internetUsage: 89.0% (consistently ranked among the top 10 fastest fixed broadband internet speeds in the world, pioneering gigabit fiber-to-the-home).
cuisine: Sarmale (national dish: seasoned minced pork, beef, and rice wrapped in fermented sauerkraut leaves or vine leaves, slow-cooked in clay pots with smoked bacon and tomato sauce, served piping hot with mămăligă / polenta, sour cream, and a fresh hot pepper / ardei iute - eaten on all holidays and weddings), Mici / Mititei (traditional grilled skinless sausages made from minced beef, pork, and lamb seasoned with garlic, thyme, anise, and sodium bicarbonate, grilled over hot charcoal and eaten with crusty bread and yellow mustard), Mămăligă (golden boiled cornmeal polenta served with brânză de burduf cheese and smântână sour cream / Bulz - baked polenta balls stuffed with cheese and bacon), Ciorbă de Burtă (traditional sour tripe soup flavored with garlic, vinegar, sour cream, and egg yolks), Ciorbă Rădăuțeană (velvety garlic-sour cream chicken soup), Salată de Boeuf, Papanași (spectacular dessert: fried cottage cheese doughnuts crowned with a dollop of thick sour cream and wild blueberry or sour cherry jam), Cozonac (festive sweet bread swirled with cocoa, walnuts, and Turkish delight), and Țuică / Pălincă (potent traditional double-distilled plum brandy, sipped before meals).
festivals: George Enescu International Classical Music Festival in Bucharest (one of the world's most prestigious classical music festivals)
Untold Festival in Cluj-Napoca (one of Europe's largest electronic dance music festivals with over 400,000 attendees)
Neversea Festival on the beach in Constanța
Sibiu International Theatre Festival (FITS - third largest performing arts festival in the world)
Transilvania International Film Festival (TIFF in Cluj-Napoca)

music: Classical genius George Enescu (Romanian Rhapsodies); Doina (deeply melancholic, improvisational traditional lyrical folk song - UNESCO); Gypsy brass virtuosos Taraf de Haïdouks (Taraful de Caliu), Fanfare Ciocărlia; pan flute maestro Gheorghe Zamfir ('The King of the Pan Flute'); dance-pop superstars (Inna, Alexandra Stan); rock legends (Phoenix, Cargo).
dance: Călușarii (ancient, hypnotic healing ritual dance featuring acrobatic leaps, jingling spurs, and wooden sticks, performed by fraternal dancers / Căluș - UNESCO), Hora (communal circle dance), Sârba, Invârtita (rapid-spinning Transylvanian couple dance).
art: Constantin Brâncuși (Father of Modern Sculpture: The Endless Column / Coloana Infinitului, The Gate of the Kiss, The Table of Silence in Târgu Jiu - inscribed on UNESCO World Heritage list in 2024); Nicolae Grigorescu (master of luminous pastoral landscapes); Theodor Aman; Victor Brauner (surrealist master); contemporary Cluj School of Art (Adrian Ghenie - one of the world's most acclaimed and sought-after contemporary painters).
architecture: Painted Monasteries of Bucovina (Voroneț Monastery with its miraculous intense lapis lazuli blue fresco - 'Voroneț Blue'); Wooden Churches of Maramureș (soaring Gothic-inspired timber spires built without nails); Transylvanian Saxon Fortified Churches (Viscri, Biertan - UNESCO); Peleș Castle in Sinaia (German Neo-Renaissance royal palace with 160 lavish rooms); Palace of the Parliament in Bucharest (Palatul Parlamentului - world's second-largest administrative building after the Pentagon, and the heaviest building on Earth); Romanian Athenaeum (Ateneul Român - neoclassical concert hall icon in Bucharest).
literature: Mihai Eminescu (National Poet: Luceafărul / The Evening Star - national romantic masterpiece), Ion Luca Caragiale (master of satirical comedy: O scrisoare pierdută), Mircea Eliade (The Myth of the Eternal Return), Eugen Ionescu (Rhinoceros, The Bald Soprano), Emil Cioran (On the Heights of Despair), Mircea Cărtărescu (visionary novelist: Solenoid, Nostalgia - multiple international literary prize winner).
cinema: Romanian New Wave (historic international Cannes festival dominance): Cristian Mungiu (Palme d'Or winner for '4 Months, 3 Weeks and 2 Days' in 2007; Graduation), Cristi Puiu (The Death of Mr. Lăzărescu), Radu Jude (Golden Bear winner at Berlin for 'Bad Luck Banging or Loony Porn' 2021), Corneliu Porumboiu (12:08 East of Bucharest).

clothing: Traditional folk attire centered on the 'Ie' (exquisite hand-embroidered peasant blouse with intricate geometric and solar patterns on linen - UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage 2022, celebrated globally on June 24 / Ziua Universală a Iei), lambskin embroidered vests (Cojoc), and black felt hats (Pălărie).

Dormition of the Virgin Mary / Navy Day (August 15)
Saint Andrew's Day (November 30 - Patron Saint of Romania)

flagDescription: Vertical tricolor of three equal bands of cobalt blue (representing freedom and clear sky), chrome yellow (representing justice and fertile grain fields), and red (representing fraternity and the blood of patriots); inspired by the revolutionary banners of the 1848 Wallachian Revolution.
coatOfArmsDescription: Azure, a golden eagle displayed, beaked and membered gules, holding in its beak an Orthodox cross or, and in its talons a sword argent and a mace or; upon its breast is a quartered shield with an inescutcheon representing the historic provinces: golden eagle of Wallachia, aurochs' head of Moldavia, lion on bridge of Banat/Oltenia, black eagle and seven castles of Transylvania, and two dolphins of Dobruja; surmounted by the Steel Crown of Romania (cast from the steel of an Ottoman cannon captured at Plevna in 1877).

politicalSituation: Centralized presidential federation governed by President Vladimir Putin and Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin; focused on strategic military-industrial mobilization, import-substitution re-industrialization, sovereign financial payments architecture (MIR system), and deepening integration with BRICS and the Global South.
foreignRelations: Permanent member of the United Nations Security Council (P5); recognized nuclear-weapon state possessing the world's largest nuclear arsenal; leading founder of BRICS (hosted the landmark expanded 16th BRICS Summit in Kazan in October 2024), Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO), Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU), and CSTO; comprehensive strategic partnership with China, India, Iran, and North Korea.
military: Armed Forces of the Russian Federation (Vooruzhyonnye Sily Rossiyskoy Federatsii: Ground Forces, Aerospace Forces, Navy, Strategic Rocket Forces / RVSN, and Airborne Forces / VDV; fully mobilized defense industrial complex producing hypersonic missiles, armored vehicles, and air defense systems).
adminDivisions: 89 federal subjects (constituent entities: 24 republics, 9 krais, 48 oblasts, 3 federal cities: Moscow, Saint Petersburg, Sevastopol, 1 autonomous oblast, and 4 autonomous okrugs)
history: East Slavic tribes united under the Rurik dynasty to form Kievan Rus' in the 9th century, accepting Eastern Orthodox Christianity under Prince Vladimir the Great in 988 AD. Fractured into principalities before the catastrophic 13th-century Mongol invasion (Golden Horde). The Grand Duchy of Moscow led the gathering of Russian lands, ending the 'Tatar yoke' at the Ugra River in 1480. Ivan IV 'the Terrible' was crowned the first Tsar of All Russia in 1547. Following the Time of Troubles, the Romanov dynasty was established in 1613. Peter the Great (reigned 1682–1725) revolutionized the state, founded Saint Petersburg on the Baltic, and proclaimed the Russian Empire in 1721. Catherine the Great expanded the empire to the Black Sea and Crimea. Defeated Napoleon's Grande Armée in the Patriotic War of 1812. The 19th century witnessed a golden age of literature, music, and science (Pushkin, Tolstoy, Dostoevsky, Tchaikovsky, Mendeleev). Strained by WWI, the 1917 Russian Revolution overthrew the Tsarist autocracy, bringing Vladimir Lenin and the Bolsheviks to power and establishing the Soviet Union (USSR) in 1922. Under Joseph Stalin, the USSR transformed via rapid industrialization and bore the primary human sacrifice in defeating Nazi Germany in the Great Patriotic War (1941–1945), losing over 27 million lives. In 1957, launched Sputnik 1 (first artificial satellite), and in 1961, sent Yuri Gagarin as the first human into outer space. After decades of Cold War superpower rivalry, the Soviet Union collapsed in December 1991. The modern Russian Federation navigated turbulent economic privatization in the 1990s, reasserting itself in the 21st century as a major global pole of geopolitical influence.
recentEvents2020_2026: Successfully hosted the historic 16th BRICS Summit in Kazan in October 2024, uniting over 30 world leaders representing the expanded BRICS bloc; maintained steady economic expansion exceeding 3.5% annually driven by domestic industrial manufacturing and sovereign trade reorientation to Asia; commissioned major Arctic LNG-2 facilities and extended the Power of Siberia gas pipeline to China; held nationwide presidential elections in March 2024.

etiquette: Direct, unpretentious, and deeply loyal; smiling is reserved for sincere personal moments rather than polite superficiality; taking off shoes and coats when entering homes; treating guests to lavish spreads of food; showing deep respect for veterans of the Great Patriotic War.

employment: Extremely low unemployment (~2.6% - historical record low); massive demand for skilled engineering, metallurgical, IT software, and agricultural logistics workers.

transport: Trans-Siberian Railway (9,289 km from Moscow to Vladivostok - longest railway line in the world) and Baikal-Amur Mainline (BAM); Moscow Metro (hailed worldwide for its palatial marble, mosaic, and chandelier stations, carrying over 9 million daily riders; Big Circle Line - BKL is the world's longest metro ring line); Northern Sea Route (icebreaker-guided Arctic shipping corridor); Russian Railways (RZhD).

internetUsage: 90.5% (dynamic domestic digital ecosystem: Yandex search, VK, Telegram founded by Pavel Durov, Gosuslugi e-governance portal, Mir payment system).
cuisine: Borscht (world-famous ruby-red beetroot soup simmered with beef, shredded cabbage, carrots, potatoes, and garlic, served with a dollop of thick sour cream / smetana and pampushki garlic bread), Pelmeni (traditional Siberian meat dumplings wrapped in thin unleavened dough, boiled and tossed in melting butter, sour cream, and black pepper), Beef Stroganoff (tender strips of beef sautéed with onions and mushrooms in a rich sour cream sauce, served over mashed potatoes or buttered egg noodles), Blini (thin golden crepes served savory with red salmon caviar, smoked sturgeon, or melted butter, or sweet with condensed milk, honey, or berry preserves), Pirozhki (baked or fried yeast buns filled with braised cabbage, minced meat, mashed potatoes, or cherries), Olivier Salad (the iconic Russian potato salad invented in Moscow in the 1860s, featuring diced potatoes, boiled eggs, carrots, pickles, green peas, and ham tossed in mayonnaise - essential on New Year's Eve), Shchi (traditional Russian cabbage soup), Kholodets (jellied pork and beef broth served with fiery horseradish and mustard), Medovik (8-layer Russian honey cake layered with tangy sour cream frosting), Syrniki (pan-fried sweet cottage cheese pancakes), Kvas (fermented rye bread beverage), and Vodka.
festivals: Victory Day (Den Pobedy on May 9 - massive military parade on Red Square and millions marching in the 'Immortal Regiment' carrying portraits of WWII veteran relatives)

music: The titan of classical music: Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky, Sergei Rachmaninoff, Igor Stravinsky (The Rite of Spring, The Firebird), Sergei Prokofiev, Dmitri Shostakovich, Modest Mussorgsky, Nikolai Rimsky-Korsakov; world-renowned conductors and soloists: Valery Gergiev, Denis Matsuev, Anna Netrebko; Russian folk instruments: Balalaika (triangular three-stringed lute), Bayan (button accordion), and Domra; legendary rock bands: Kino (Viktor Tsoi), DDT, Aquarium.
dance: The undisputed world capital of classical ballet: The Bolshoi Ballet (Moscow) and Mariinsky Ballet (Saint Petersburg); ballet legends: Rudolf Nureyev, Mikhail Baryshnikov, Anna Pavlova, Maya Plisetskaya, Galina Ulanova; legendary folk dance companies: Igor Moiseyev Ballet, Beryozka Ensemble (famed for its floating gliding step where women in floor-length gowns appear stationary while drifting across the stage).
art: Icon painting: Andrei Rublev (The Trinity); Realism of the Peredvizhniki (Wanderers): Ilya Repin (Barge Haulers on the Volga, Reply of the Zaporozhian Cossacks), Ivan Aivazovsky (master of turbulent seascapes: The Ninth Wave), Ivan Shishkin (master of Russian pine forests); Russian Avant-Garde: Kazimir Malevich (Black Square - pioneer of Suprematism), Wassily Kandinsky (pioneer of pure abstraction), Marc Chagall, Natalia Goncharova; Tretyakov Gallery and Hermitage Museum.
architecture: Russian Orthodox architecture: Onion domes (designed to prevent snow accumulation and symbolize burning prayer candles: Saint Basil's Cathedral on Red Square, Cathedral of Christ the Saviour); Saint Petersburg Baroque and Neoclassicism: Winter Palace (Hermitage) by Bartolomeo Rastrelli, Peterhof Grand Palace with 64 fountains, Saint Isaac's Cathedral; Moscow Kremlin (red-brick medieval fortress walls and Spasskaya clock tower); Seven Sisters (Stalinist Gothic skyscrapers, including Moscow State University); modern marvels: Lakhta Center in Saint Petersburg (462 m - tallest skyscraper in Europe).

flagDescription: Horizontal tricolor of three equal bands of white (top, symbolizing nobility and frankness), blue (middle, symbolizing loyalty, honesty, and chastity), and red (bottom, symbolizing courage, generosity, and love); originally introduced by Peter the Great in 1696 for merchant shipping, restored as national flag in 1991.
coatOfArmsDescription: Gules, a golden double-headed eagle displayed, crowned with three imperial crowns (two smaller and one larger above, linked by a ribbon), holding in its dexter talon a golden sceptre and in its sinister talon a golden globus cruciger; on its breast is an escutcheon gules depicting a silver knight (Saint George) in blue armour, riding a silver horse and slaying a black dragon with a silver spear.

name: San Marino
capital: City of San Marino (Città di San Marino)

motto: Libertas (Liberty)
borders: Italy (enclave surrounded completely by Emilia-Romagna and Marche regions)
coastline: 0 km (landlocked enclave)
highestPoint: Monte Titano (739 m - three-peaked limestone ridge crowning the country)
longestRiver: San Marino River (Marano - 16 km total, 8 km in San Marino) and Ausa River
majorLakes: Lago di Faetano (artificial recreational fishing lake)

politicalSituation: Harmonious direct republic governed under ancient consular traditions; finalized historic EU Association Agreement negotiations in late 2023–2024, integrating San Marino into the EU Single Market while preserving national sovereignty; stable multi-party democracy.
foreignRelations: Member of the United Nations (joined 1992), Council of Europe (joined 1988), OSCE, and WTO; concluded negotiations for an Association Agreement with the European Union in December 2023; historic open-border relationship with Italy governed by the 1939 Friendship Treaty.
military: Voluntary ceremonial and defense units: Military Corps of San Marino (Corpi Militari: Crossbow Corps / Balestrieri, Guard of the Rock / Guardia di Rocca, Uniformed Militia, and Guardia del Consiglio Grande e Generale); civil police provided by the Polizia Civile and Gendarmeria.
adminDivisions: 9 municipalities (castelli: Acquaviva, Borgo Maggiore, Chiesanuova, Domagnano, Faetano, Fiorentino, Montegiardino, San Marino, Serravalle)
history: Founded on September 3, 301 AD, by Saint Marinus (San Marino), a Christian stonemason fleeing religious persecution on the island of Rab (modern Croatia). Marinus established a small Christian community atop Mount Titano with the legendary dying words: 'Relinquo vos liberos ab utroque homine' (I leave you free from both men - referring to the Pope and the Emperor), establishing the foundation of freedom and independence. Preserved its communal independence through the Middle Ages, codifying its municipal laws into the Statutes of 1600. When Napoleon conquered Italy in 1797, he was so impressed by San Marino's ancient republican virtue that he offered to expand its territory (which the prudent Sammarinese politely declined, wishing to preserve their peace). Sheltered Giuseppe Garibaldi during the Italian Risorgimento in 1849; in gratitude, unified Italy guaranteed San Marino's perpetual sovereignty in 1862. Abraham Lincoln famously accepted honorary citizenship in 1861, calling San Marino 'one of the most honored in all history'. Remained neutral in both World Wars, sheltering over 100,000 refugees during WWII.
recentEvents2020_2026: Finalized the landmark Association Agreement with the European Union alongside Andorra in December 2023, advancing full integration into the European Single Market; celebrated national sporting euphoria as San Marino won three Olympic medals at the Tokyo Olympics (including silver in trap shooting for Alessandra Perilli - becoming the smallest country in Olympic history to win a medal); achieved its historic first competitive international football victory in 20 years by defeating Liechtenstein in the UEFA Nations League in September 2024; maintained smooth biannual transitions of the Captains Regent.

etiquette: Polite, proud of independence, and warm; distinguishing Sammarinese citizenship from Italian identity; courteous greetings; dressing respectfully when entering government buildings and the Basilica of Saint Marinus.

tourism: Charming cultural and medieval heritage tourism hosting over 2 million visitors annually: exploring the Three Towers of San Marino (Guaita, Cesta, Montale) connected by the panoramic Witch's Path (Passo delle Streghe), the Piazza della Libertà and Public Palace (Palazzo Pubblico), riding the scenic aerial funicular from Borgo Maggiore, tax-free boutique shopping, and visiting philatelic and coin museums.
employment: Extremely high employment rate, virtually zero long-term unemployment (~2.2%); substantial daily commuter influx of thousands of Italian workers from neighboring Emilia-Romagna and Marche.
debtInflation: Sound public finances with low debt-to-GDP; AAA/AA credit profile; price stability guaranteed by use of the Euro within the Eurosystem.
transport: Funivia di San Marino (panoramic aerial cable car linking Borgo Maggiore to the City of San Marino atop Monte Titano); Superstrada di San Marino (SS72 connecting directly to Rimini and the Italian A14 motorway); modern public bus network (AASP); historic railway tunnel museum (Trenino Bianco).
airports: No commercial airport within the territory; served by Federico Fellini International Airport in Rimini, Italy (RMI, 16 km away) and Bologna Guglielmo Marconi Airport (BLQ, 130 km away); Torraccia Heliport handles private helicopter transfers.
ports: None (landlocked; commercial maritime freight handled through the Port of Ravenna and Port of Ancona on the Italian Adriatic coast).
internetUsage: 96.5% (world's first country with 100% nationwide 5G mobile coverage, deployed by Telecom Italia San Marino).
cuisine: Torta Tre Monti (famous signature dessert: delicate round wafer layers filled with rich chocolate and hazelnut cream, coated around the rim with dark chocolate fondant - certified traditional product), Piadina (warm, flaky thin flatbread griddled on a clay plate, stuffed with prosciutto, fresh squacquerone cheese, and wild arugula), Strozzapreti (traditional hand-rolled elongated pasta twists served with savory meat ragù or wild mushrooms), Cappelletti in brodo (delicate stuffed pasta parcels served in rich steaming capon broth), Nidi di rondine (baked pasta 'swallow's nests' rolled with ham, cheese, and bechamel), Polenta con le beccafiche (polenta served with savory wild bird or pork sauce), Bustrengo (traditional dense sweet cake made with cornmeal, breadcrumbs, apples, raisins, dried figs, and lemon zest), and fine Sammarinese wines: Sangiovese, Tessano, and Moscato di San Marino (sweet aromatic dessert wine).

literature: Marino Fattori (19th-century author of 'Ricordi Storici della Repubblica di San Marino'), historical chronicles, modern poetry and cultural essays published by the Centro Sammarinese di Studi Storici.
cinema: San Marino Film Festival; featured location in international historical films; San Marino RTV film documentaries.
sports: Shooting Sports (legendary Olympic superpower: Alessandra Perilli - Olympic Silver Tokyo 2020 in women's trap shooting; Gian Marco Berti and Alessandra Perilli - Olympic Bronze in mixed team trap; historic first Olympic medals for San Marino); Motorsport (San Marino Grand Prix at Imola historically, and the San Marino and Rimini's Coast MotoGP Grand Prix held at nearby Misano World Circuit; Rally di San Marino); Football (San Marino national football team; historical UEFA Nations League victory in 2024; Campionato Sammarinese di Calcio: Tre Penne, La Fiorita); Baseball (T&A San Marino - multiple Italian and European Champions).

flagDescription: Two equal horizontal bands of white (top, symbolizing peace and the snow on Monte Titano) and light blue (bottom, symbolizing liberty and the blue sky above the republic), charged in the center with the national Coat of Arms of San Marino.
coatOfArmsDescription: Azure, three green hills (the three summits of Monte Titano), each crowned with a silver tower bearing an ostrich feather (the Three Towers of San Marino: Guaita, Cesta, Montale); the shield is surrounded by a laurel branch on the left and an oak branch on the right, surmounted by a closed golden crown (symbol of sovereignty), with a white scroll beneath bearing the national motto 'LIBERTAS' (Liberty).

shortSummary: San Marino is the world's oldest surviving constitutional republic, founded in 301 AD atop the three craggy limestone towers of Mount Titano, celebrated for its 1,700-year devotion to freedom (Libertas), medieval crossbow pageantry, tax-free charm, and panoramic views of the Adriatic.

Climate: Humid subtropical transitioning to Mediterranean; warm, sunny summers and cool, crisp winters with occasional mountain snow blanketing the three medieval towers atop Monte Titano.

history: Settled by Slavs in the 6th–7th centuries; the Grand Principality of Serbia emerged under Stefan Nemanja in the 12th century, founding the Nemanjić dynasty. His son, Saint Sava, established the autocephalous Serbian Orthodox Church in 1219. Reached its imperial golden age under Emperor Stefan Dušan the Mighty (Dušan's Code, 1349). Following the epic Battle of Kosovo (June 28, 1389 - Vidovdan) and the fall of Smederevo in 1459, Serbia was incorporated into the Ottoman Empire for over four centuries. The First Serbian Uprising of 1804 led by Karađorđe and the Second Uprising of 1815 led by Miloš Obrenović restored autonomous statehood, recognized as fully independent at the 1878 Congress of Berlin. Survived immense human sacrifice in WWI, losing over 25% of its total population while repelling Austro-Hungarian forces and breaking the Macedonian Front. Founded the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes in 1918 (later Yugoslavia). Resisted Axis occupation in WWII, re-emerging as the central republic of socialist Yugoslavia under Josip Broz Tito, with Belgrade as the federal capital and birthplace of the Non-Aligned Movement. Following the painful breakup of Yugoslavia in the 1990s, Serbia democratized in the peaceful October 2000 overthrow of Slobodan Milošević, transforming into a vibrant modern IT and manufacturing engine.

Kustendorf Film and Music Festival in Drvengrad (founded by Emir Kusturica)
music: Balkan Brass Band music (fiery, exhilarating virtuoso trumpet music popularized by Boban Marković and Goran Bregović); traditional Tamburica orchestras of Vojvodina (Janika Balaž, Zvonko Bogdan); rock legends (Riblja Čorba, Ekatarina Velika / EKV, Bajaga i Instruktori, Partibrejkers); classical violin masters: Stefan Milenkovich, Nemanja Radulović; folk icons: Šaban Šaulić, Ceca.
dance: Kolo (traditional collective circle dance performed by dancers holding hands in vibrant rhythmic circular movements accompanied by accordion and frula - UNESCO), Moravac, Užičko kolo, Čačak.
art: Medieval fresco masterpieces: The White Angel (Beli Anđeo in Mileševa Monastery, 1230s - universally celebrated for its Renaissance-anticipating serenity, beamed into outer space in early satellite transmissions); Paja Jovanović (monumental historical paintings: The Migration of the Serbs); Uroš Predić; Nadežda Petrović (pioneer of Serbian modernism and war nurse); Marina Abramović (the 'Grandmother of Performance Art' - global contemporary art titan, born in Belgrade).
architecture: Serbo-Byzantine architectural style: Raška school (Studenica Monastery, Žiča), Morava school (Kalenić, Manasija); Church of Saint Sava in Belgrade (Hram Svetog Save - one of the largest Orthodox church buildings in the world, crowned with a massive dome and over 15,000 m² of breathtaking golden mosaics); Petrovaradin Fortress ('Gibraltar on the Danube'); Kalemegdan Fortress; brutalist modernist masterpieces of New Belgrade (Western City Gate / Genex Tower, Palace of Serbia).
literature: Ivo Andrić (Nobel Prize in Literature 1961: The Bridge on the Drina / Na Drini ćuprija, Bosnian Chronicle), Miloš Crnjanski (Migrations / Seobe), Danilo Kiš (A Tomb for Boris Davidovich), Milorad Pavić (Dictionary of the Khazars - landmark nonlinear interactive novel translated into 40 languages), Borislav Pekić, Dobrica Ćosić.
cinema: Emir Kusturica (two-time Cannes Palme d'Or winner: When Father Was Away on Business 1985, Underground 1995; Black Cat, White Cat); Dušan Kovačević (famed playwright and screenwriter: The Marathon Family, Who's Singin' Over There? / Ko to tamo peva - widely voted the greatest Yugoslav film of all time); contemporary cinema: 'Dardania', 'The Load', 'Guardians of the Formula' (Dragan Bjelogrlić).
sports: The undisputed sporting capital of the world per capita: Tennis (Novak Djokovic - the GOAT: all-time record 24 Grand Slam men's singles titles, 428+ weeks as world #1, Career Golden Slam with 2024 Olympic Gold in Paris; Davis Cup Champions), Basketball (undisputed global powerhouse: Nikola Jokić - three-time NBA MVP 2021, 2022, 2024 and 2023 NBA Champion with Denver Nuggets; Bogdan Bogdanović; 2024 Olympic Bronze medalists in Paris; KK Partizan and KK Crvena Zvezda EuroLeague dynasties), Water Polo (Delfini - legendary three-time consecutive Olympic Gold Champions: Rio 2016, Tokyo 2020, Paris 2024), Volleyball (Women's National Team: double World Champions 2018, 2022; Tijana Bošković), Football (Dragan Stojković Piksi, Nemanja Vidić, Dušan Vlahović, Aleksandar Mitrović).
media: RTS (Radio Televizija Srbije - public broadcaster: RTS 1, RTS 2, RTS 3), RTV (Radio Television of Vojvodina), TV Pink, Prva TV, N1 Info, Politika (founded 1904 - oldest surviving daily newspaper in the Balkans), Večernje novosti, Blic, Danas, Tanjug news agency.
clothing: Traditional Serbian folk dress (Narodna nošnja): Šajkača (traditional wool V-shaped cap worn with pride by men), Opanci (traditional pigskin or leather moccasin shoes with distinctive curved horn-like upturned toes), embroidered white linen shirts (košulja), handwoven wool aprons (kecelja), and thick wool waistcoats (jelek) trimmed with golden cord; modern cosmopolitan urban style.
holidays: New Year's Day (January 1-2) and Orthodox / Old New Year (Srpska Nova Godina - January 13-14)
Orthodox Christmas (Božić - January 7, with Badnjak oak branch ceremonies)
Armistice Day in WWI (November 11 - wearing the purple Ramonda serbica flower)
crafts: Pirot kilim handweaving (Pirotski ćilim - world-famous flatwoven wool tapestries with 122 geometric protective motifs - UNESCO national list), Zlakusa pottery (handcrafted clay and calcite pottery made on slow wheels and fired over open wood fires - UNESCO), woodcarving, plum brandy distillation.
worldHeritageSites: Stari Ras and Sopoćani (1979 - 13th-century Byzantine frescoes in the original medieval capital)
Studenica Monastery (1986 - mother church of all Serbian monasteries, founded 1190 by Stefan Nemanja)
Medieval Monuments in Kosovo (Dečani, Peć, Gračanica, Ljeviš - 2004/2006)
Gamzigrad-Romuliana, Palace of Galerius (2007 - fortified late Roman imperial palace)
Stećci Medieval Tombstones Graveyards (transboundary)
unescoIntangible: Slava, celebration of family saint's patron day (2014 - first Serbian inscription)
Singing to the accompaniment of the Gusle (2018)
Social practices and knowledge related to the preparation and use of the traditional plum spirit - Šljivovica (2022)
flagDescription: Horizontal tricolor of three equal bands of red (top, representing the blood shed for freedom), blue (middle, representing the sky of freedom), and white (bottom, representing dazzling light and purity); charged with the lesser Coat of Arms of Serbia shifted towards the hoist.
coatOfArmsDescription: Gules, a double-headed eagle argent with golden beaks and talons, bearing on its breast an escutcheon gules with a silver cross between four silver firesteels (Serbian cross with the four Cyrillic 'S' letters: Samo Sloga Srbina Spasava); below the eagle sit two golden fleur-de-lis, and above rests the royal crown of Serbia, draped in an ermine-lined royal mantle.

symbols.flower: Serbian ramonda (Natalijina ramonda - 'phoenix flower' capable of reviving when watered, symbol of WWI resilience)

landmarks: Church of Saint Sava (Belgrade - one of the world's largest Orthodox cathedrals)
Belgrade Fortress and Kalemegdan Park (overlooking Danube-Sava confluence)

travelNotes: Stand inside the awe-inspiring interior of Saint Sava Temple in Belgrade, surrounded by 15,000 square meters of shimmering gold mosaic; watch the sun set over the confluence of the Sava and Danube from the stone battlements of Kalemegdan Fortress; gaze down upon the emerald serpentine loops of the Uvac River Canyon as giant griffon vultures soar overhead; savor sizzling pljeskavica and warm kajmak in a Skadarlija kafana to the sounds of live tamburica music; dance until dawn at EXIT Festival inside Petrovaradin Fortress.
shortSummary: Serbia is a dynamic Balkan powerhouse at the crossroads of Central and Southeast Europe, famed for the vibrant nightlife and towering Saint Sava cathedral of Belgrade, UNESCO medieval monasteries like Studenica, delicious grilled ćevapi and šljivovica, and all-time sporting titans like Nikola Tesla, Novak Djokovic, and Nikola Jokić.
geography: Spanning 77,474 km² across Southern Europe / Balkans. Highest point: Midžor (2,169 m in the Balkan Mountains / Stara Planina on the border with Bulgaria); lowest point: Danube River and Timok mouth (28 m). Longest river: Danube River (588 km in Serbia - flowing past Belgrade and the dramatic Iron Gates gorge / Đerdap), West Morava (308 km), South Morava (295 km), Great Morava (185 km), and Sava River (206 km in Serbia). Climate: Moderate continental climate with four distinct seasons: warm summers, crisp autumns, and cold, snowy winters in the mountains; moderated by Pannonian continental air in Vojvodina and mountain breezes in Šumadija.
economy: Economy with GDP nominal of $86 billion (approx. 2026) ($13,100 (over $28,000 PPP) per capita). Leading sectors: Services 66%, Industry 26%, Agriculture 8%. Main industries: Information technology, software engineering, and gaming (Belgrade and Novi Sad tech clusters: Microsoft Development Center Serbia, Nordeus - Top Eleven, Schneider Electric DMS), Automotive manufacturing and electric vehicle production (Stellantis factory in Kragujevac producing the electric Fiat Grande Panda; tire giants: Michelin Tigar, Linglong), Mining and copper metallurgy (Serbia Zijin Copper in Bor - one of Europe's largest copper and gold complexes), Heavy machinery, agricultural tractors, and defense equipment (Yugoimport SDPR - Nora B-52 howitzers, Lazar armored vehicles), Chemicals, fertilizers, and plastics (HIP-Petrohemija), Food and beverage processing (Bambi, Štark, Knjaz Miloš, Jelen and Zaječarsko beer). Key exports: Electrical machinery, wiring, and vehicle components, Refined copper cathodes and gold, Electric and hybrid motor vehicles (Fiat Grande Panda), Agricultural commodities (corn, wheat, frozen raspberries, apples), Tires and rubber products, IT software and digital gaming services, Iron, steel, and defense materiel.
culture: Rich cultural traditions featuring cuisine (Ćevapi / Ćevapčići (grilled minced meat sausages made from seasoned beef and pork, served in warm somun bread with raw diced onions and rich kajmak clotted cream), Pljeskavica (the legendary Serbian gourmet burger: seasoned beef and pork patty stuffed with cheese and smoked ham / Gurmanska pljeskavica), Sarma (pickled cabbage leaves stuffed with minced meat, rice, and smoked pork ribs, slow-cooked in clay pots - staple of winter and slava feasts), Karađorđeva Šnicla (veal or pork schnitzel rolled around rich kajmak, breaded, fried golden brown, and served with tartar sauce - nicknamed 'the maiden's dream'), Kajmak (unctuous, creamy clotted dairy spread made from simmering unpasteurized cow's milk), Prebranac (baked white beans with caramelized onions and sweet paprika), Gibanica (traditional flaky egg and cheese pastry pie made with cottage cheese and kajmak), Pečenje (whole roast suckling pig or lamb carved fresh off the spit), Ajvar (roasted red pepper caviar), and Šljivovica (the revered national plum brandy, aged in oak casks for years - inscribed on UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2022).), traditional music and dance (Balkan Brass Band music (fiery, exhilarating virtuoso trumpet music popularized by Boban Marković and Goran Bregović); traditional Tamburica orchestras of Vojvodina (Janika Balaž, Zvonko Bogdan); rock legends (Riblja Čorba, Ekatarina Velika / EKV, Bajaga i Instruktori, Partibrejkers); classical violin masters: Stefan Milenkovich, Nemanja Radulović; Davis Cup Champions), Basketball (undisputed global powerhouse: Nikola Jokić - three-time NBA MVP 2021, 2022, 2024 and 2023 NBA Champion with Denver Nuggets; Bogdan Bogdanović; 2024 Olympic Bronze medalists in Paris; KK Partizan and KK Crvena Zvezda EuroLeague dynasties), Water Polo (Delfini - legendary three-time consecutive Olympic Gold Champions: Rio 2016, Tokyo 2020, Paris 2024), Volleyball (Women's National Team: double World Champions 2018, 2022; name: Slovakia
nationalDay: January 1 (Day of the Establishment of the Slovak Republic in 1993) and August 29 (Slovak National Uprising Day 1944)
nationalAnthem: Nad Tatrou sa blýska (Lightning over the Tatras)
motto: None
coastline: 0 km (landlocked)
highestPoint: Gerlachovský štít (2,655 m in the High Tatras - highest peak in the Carpathian Mountains)
longestRiver: Váh River (406 km entirely in Slovakia) and Danube River (172 km bordering in the southwest)
majorLakes: Štrbské Pleso (famous alpine glacial tarn in the High Tatras)
Veľké Hincovo pleso (deepest natural tarn, 53 m)
majorMountains: Carpathian Mountains: High Tatras (Vysoké Tatry), Low Tatras (Nízke Tatry), Malá Fatra, Veľká Fatra, Slovak Ore Mountains (Slovenské rudohorie), Slovak Paradise (Slovenský raj)
climate: Temperate continental climate with warm summers and cold, snowy winters; significant alpine conditions across the High and Low Tatras with ski seasons lasting into late spring
naturalHazards: Seasonal mountain avalanches and winter freeze in the Tatras
Localized river flooding along the Danube, Váh, and Hron basins during spring melts
environmentalIssues: Transitioning from industrial lignite mining in Upper Nitra (completed coal phase-out 2023)
Preserving ancient Carpathian beech forests from excessive timber harvesting
Air quality improvements in valley basins
biodiversity: Spectacular biodiversity across 9 national parks: High Tatras National Park (TANAP - oldest national park in Slovakia, established 1949), Slovak Paradise with deep limestone ravines and waterfalls; sanctuary for the endemic Tatra chamois (Rupicapra rupicapra tatrica), brown bears (~1,200), Eurasian lynx, grey wolves, Tatra marmots, and golden eagles
languages: Slovak (official West Slavic language, often termed the 'Slavic Esperanto' due to its central phonetic comprehensibility across Slavic languages)
Hungarian (recognized minority language spoken by ~8% in southern border areas)
currency: Euro (EUR, € - adopted January 1, 2009; former Slovak Koruna)
legislature: National Council of the Slovak Republic (Národná rada Slovenskej republiky - unicameral, 150 seats)
latestElections: Parliamentary election September 2023 (coalition government formed under Robert Fico); presidential election April 2024 (electing Peter Pellegrini); European election June 2024; next general election scheduled 2027
politicalSituation: Parliamentary democracy navigated by Prime Minister Robert Fico and President Peter Pellegrini; focused on economic re-industrialization, energy sovereignty via nuclear expansion, and navigating European integration; world leader in per capita automotive production.
foreignRelations: Member of European Union (joined 2004), NATO (joined 2004), Eurozone (joined 2009), Schengen Area (joined 2007), Visegrád Group (V4), OECD, WTO, and Council of Europe; close bilateral alliance with neighboring Czechia following the peaceful 1993 'Velvet Divorce'.
military: Armed Forces of the Slovak Republic (Ozbrojené sily Slovenskej republiky: Ground Forces, Air Force; deploying F-16 Block 70 multirole fighters, CV90 infantry fighting vehicles, and Zuzana 2 self-propelled howitzers).
adminDivisions: 8 administrative regions (kraje: Bratislava, Trnava, Trenčín, Nitra, Žilina, Banská Bystrica, Prešov, Košice) divided into 79 districts (okresy)
history: Slavic tribes settled the region in the 5th–6th centuries; part of Samo's Empire (623 AD) and the Principality of Nitra under Prince Pribina, who consecrated the first Christian church in Slavic territory in 828 AD. Merged into Great Moravia in 833 AD, which welcomed Byzantine missionaries Saints Cyril and Methodius in 863 AD. Following the fall of Great Moravia, Slovakia was incorporated into the Kingdom of Hungary for a thousand years (Upper Hungary / Horná Zem). When the Ottomans occupied Buda in 1541, Bratislava (Pozsony / Pressburg) became the coronation capital of the Kingdom of Hungary for nearly 300 years, crowning 11 Habsburg kings and queens (including Maria Theresa) in St. Martin's Cathedral. In the 19th century, Ľudovít Štúr codified the modern literary Slovak language. Joined Czechs in 1918 to form the democratic first Czechoslovak Republic. During WWII, the puppet Slovak State was defied by the heroic 1944 Slovak National Uprising (SNP) centered in Banská Bystrica. After decades of communist rule within Czechoslovakia and the 1989 Velvet Revolution, Slovakia achieved peaceful independence on January 1, 1993 (the 'Velvet Divorce'). Transformed dynamically through the 'Tatra Tiger' economic reforms into the world's premier car manufacturing capital per capita.
recentEvents2020_2026: Inaugurated Peter Pellegrini as President of Slovakia in June 2024 following the presidential election; commissioned Unit 3 of the Mochovce Nuclear Power Plant (471 MW VVER-440 reactor), transforming Slovakia into a 100% self-sufficient clean nuclear power exporter; finalized construction of the massive €1.2 billion Volvo Cars electric vehicle gigafactory in Valaliky near Košice (Slovakia's fifth major automotive manufacturing plant); completed the phase-out of all coal-fired electricity generation in late 2023.
historicalFigures: Saints Cyril and Methodius (Apostles to the Slavs)
Prince Pribina (ruler of the Principality of Nitra)
Ľudovít Štúr (national leader who codified the modern Slovak language)
Milan Rastislav Štefánik (astronomer, French Army general, and co-founder of Czechoslovakia)
Alexander Dubček (leader of the 1968 Prague Spring - 'Socialism with a Human Face')
Andy Warhol (Andrew Warhola - global Pop Art icon whose parents emigrated from Miková, Slovakia)
Jozef Murgaš (pioneer of wireless telegraphy and radio)
Peter Sagan (cycling superstar - historic three-time consecutive UCI World Road Race Champion)
Zuzana Čaputová (first female President of Slovakia, served 2019–2024)
religions: Evangelical Church of the Augsburg Confession (Lutheran) ~5.3%
education: Comenius University in Bratislava (Univerzita Komenského - founded 1919, premier national university), Slovak University of Technology in Bratislava (STU), Technical University of Košice (TUKE), Pavol Jozef Šafárik University in Košice; strong engineering, cybernetics, and automotive R&D clusters.
healthcare: Universal statutory health insurance through one public (VšZP) and two private health insurance companies; University Hospital Bratislava (UNB), University Hospital Martin, and specialized National Institute of Cardiovascular Diseases (NÚSCH).
socialCustoms: Chata culture (weekend escapes to wooden alpine cottages in the mountains for hiking, skiing, and wood-stove fires), autumn wild mushroom foraging (hubárčenie), Easter Monday tradition of gentle willow whipping (šibačka) and water splashing (oblievačka) accompanied by chocolate eggs, drinking warm hriatô (spiced honey bacon schnapps) in winter.
etiquette: Polite, modest, and hospitable; greeting with a firm handshake or double-cheek kiss; removing shoes at the front door and slipping into house slippers (papuče); bringing wine, quality spirits, or flowers (odd numbers only) when visiting; raising a glass with 'Na zdravie!' (To health!).
nationalIdentity: Defined by dramatic mountain landscapes (High Tatras), hundreds of fairy-tale stone castles, the sacred heritage of Saints Cyril and Methodius, shepherd mountain folklore (Bryndza cheese and the Fujara flute), and engineering excellence in global automotive manufacturing.
industries: Automotive manufacturing (undisputed world champion in cars produced per capita: over 1 million vehicles produced annually across four major auto plants: Volkswagen Slovakia in Bratislava, Stellantis in Trnava, Kia Motors in Žilina, Jaguar Land Rover in Nitra, plus the new Volvo Cars all-electric megasite in Košice)
Information technology and cybersecurity (ESET - global cybersecurity titan and maker of NOD32 antivirus; Pixel Federation - game software)
Electrical engineering and consumer electronics (Samsung Electronics, Foxconn)
Metallurgy and steel production (U.S. Steel Košice - major blast furnace steel complex)
Machinery, industrial robotics, and defense equipment (ZVS Holding, Konstrukta Defence - Zuzana howitzers)
Chemicals, plastics, and pharmaceutical manufacturing (Slovnaft oil refinery, Duslo Šaľa)
agriculture: Wheat, barley (malting barley for brewing), and maize / corn in the southern Danubian lowlands
Sugar beets and sunflowers
Oilseed rape / Canola
Dairy farming and sheep breeding (world-famous Bryndza sheep cheese)
Wine viticulture (Small Carpathian wine region, Tokaj region shared with Hungary)
Forestry and timber processing
naturalResources: Abundant mineral springs and thermal thermal spas (over 1,600 natural springs)
Limestone, dolomite, and magnesite (world's #3 producer of magnesite)
Extensive timber forests covering over 41% of land area
Arable fertile soils in the Danubian and East Slovak lowlands
energy: Over 85% carbon-free electricity: Nuclear power superpower: Mochovce and Bohunice nuclear plants generating over 62% of domestic electricity (second highest nuclear share in the world after France, with Mochovce Unit 4 commissioning), Hydroelectric power (Gabčíkovo dam on the Danube and pumped-storage plants like Čierny Váh generating ~16%), expanding solar PV and biomass; 100% phased out domestic coal mining in 2023.
exports: Motor vehicles, SUVs, and automotive components (representing over 45% of total merchandise exports)
Electrical machinery, televisions, and electronic equipment
Iron, steel, and flat-rolled metal products
imports: Machinery, mechanical appliances, and electrical parts for auto assembly
Motor vehicle parts and electronic components
Crude petroleum and natural gas (via Druzhba and European interconnectors)
tourism: Over 6 million visitors captivated by dramatic mountain peaks in the High Tatras, fairy-tale castles (Bojnice Castle, Spiš Castle - one of Europe's largest castle ruins), hiking through the wooden ladders and waterfalls of Slovak Paradise (Slovenský raj), exploring Bratislava's compact Old Town along the Danube, world-class thermal water spas (Piešťany), and the icy subterranean wonder of Dobšinská Ice Cave.
employment: Extremely high industrial manufacturing and engineering employment, dynamic IT clusters in Bratislava and Košice, low national unemployment (~5.4%).
debtInflation: Monetary policy steered by the European Central Bank (ECB) with the National Bank of Slovakia (Národná banka Slovenska - NBS) ensuring domestic financial stability; public debt-to-GDP around 57%.
transport: Radial motorway network (D1 connecting Bratislava across the country toward Košice, D2 linking Czechia to Hungary, R1 express highway); ŽSR national railway network operating fast modern electric trains; Danube river shipping connecting to the Black Sea and North Sea.
airports: M. R. Štefánik Airport Bratislava (BTS - capital airport, complemented by Vienna International Airport Schwechat located only 45 km away)
Poprad-Tatry Airport (TAT - highest commercial airport in Central Europe, 718 m, serving the High Tatras)
ports: Major commercial river ports on the Danube: Port of Bratislava and Port of Komárno (handling dry bulk, grain, and petroleum products connecting to international maritime corridors).
internetUsage: 90.2% (ubiquitous high-speed broadband and 5G network coverage).
cuisine: Bryndzové Halušky (the beloved national dish: small soft potato dumplings / gnocchi tossed with creamy, tangy unpasteurized sheep milk Bryndza cheese, smothered in crispy golden smoked bacon cubes / škvarky, and drizzled with hot bacon drippings, traditionally washed down with a glass of sour sheep milk / žinčica), Bryndzové Pirohy (crescent-shaped potato dough pockets stuffed with bryndza and mashed potatoes, topped with bacon and sour cream), Kapustnica (rich, comforting Christmas and winter soup made from fermented sauerkraut, smoked pork sausages, smoked ham, dried forest porcini mushrooms, and prunes), Vyprážaný syr (crispy breaded fried cheese served with French fries and tartar sauce), Zemiakové placky (crispy garlic and marjoram potato pancakes), Gulášová polievka (hearty goulash soup cooked in an outdoor cauldron / kotlík), Skalický trdelník (spit-roasted sweet walnut pastry roll with PDO/PGI European status), Bratislavské rožky (crescent rolls filled with sweet poppy seeds or crushed walnuts), and iconic drinks: Kofola (beloved Czechoslovak herbal cola with 14 natural fruit and herbal ingredients, created in 1960), Tatratea (legendary herbal tea liqueur from the High Tatras, with strengths from 22% to 72%), Borovička (juniper berry spirit), and crisp Slovak lager beers (Zlatý Bažant / Golden Pheasant, Šariš).
festivals: Východná Folklore Festival (held every July in the village of Východná beneath Mount Kriváň - oldest and largest folklore festival in Slovakia with thousands of performers)
Pohoda Festival in Trenčín (award-winning, beloved multi-genre open-air music and arts festival held on Trenčín airfield)
Bratislava Coronation Days (historical reenactments of Hungarian royal coronations in St. Martin's Cathedral)
Kremnica Gags (European festival of humor and satire)
Cibula Fest (cross-border music festival)
music: The Fujara (monumental, deep-toned, over-2-meter-long traditional wooden overtone bass flute played by shepherds, declared by UNESCO as a Masterpiece of Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity in 2005); classical composer Eugen Suchoň (Krútňava - national opera), Ján Cikker; Slovak Philharmonic Orchestra; pop/rock icons (Elán, Miroslav Žbirka, Richard Müller, IMT Smile, Horkýže Slíže).
dance: Traditional folk dances: Odzemok (acrobatic shepherd axe dance with shepherds' hatchets / valaška), Karička (whirlwind female circle dance of eastern Slovakia), Čardáš (passionate couple dance with dizzying spins); modern contemporary dance company Divadlo Štúdio tanca in Banská Bystrica.
art: Andy Warhol (Pop Art titan: Campbell's Soup Cans, Marilyn Monroe - celebrated at the Andy Warhol Museum of Modern Art in Medzilaborce, the second museum in the world dedicated to his work); Ľudovít Fulla (pioneering modernist painter blending folk motifs with avant-garde); Martin Benka (monumental romantic depictions of Slovak mountain life); Albín Brunovský (master of fantastic realism and graphic printmaking).
architecture: Master Paul of Levoča (Late Gothic woodcarver who created the world's tallest wooden Gothic altar in St. James's Church in Levoča, 18.6 m high - UNESCO); Castle architecture (Slovakia has one of the highest concentrations of castles per capita in the world: over 180 castles and 425 châteaux: Spiš Castle, Bojnice Romantic Castle, Orava Castle perched on a 112 m cliff, Trenčín Castle); Folk wooden architecture: Čičmany (famous village of dark timber houses decorated with white geometric embroidery-like lime paintings), Vlkolínec (UNESCO preserved mountain log-cabin hamlet); modern landmarks: UFO Bridge (Most SNP in Bratislava with a flying-saucer-shaped observation deck and restaurant 85 m above the Danube).
literature: Pavol Országh Hviezdoslav (National Poet: The Forester's Wife / Hájnikova žena, Bloody Sonnets), Ľudovít Štúr, Martin Kukučín, Jozef Cíger-Hronský, Ladislav Mňačko (The Taste of Power), contemporary authors: Pavel Vilikovský, Daniela Capitáňová.
cinema: Czechoslovak New Wave masterpieces: 'The Shop on Main Street' (Obchod na korze - directed by Ján Kadár and Elmar Klos, set in Sabinov, Slovakia - won the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film in 1965); Juraj Jakubisko ('The Fellini of the East': The Millennial Bee, Birds, Orphans and Fools); Dušan Hanák (Pictures of the Old World); contemporary cinema: 'The Line' (Čiara - Peter Bebjak), 'The Interpreter' (Martin Šulík).
sports: Ice hockey (undisputed national religion: 2002 IIHF World Champions, historic Olympic Bronze medal at Beijing 2022; NHL legends Peter Šťastný, Stan Mikita, Marián Hossa - Hall of Famer, Marián Gáborík, Zdeno Chára - tallest player in NHL history, Juraj Slafkovský - #1 overall NHL draft pick 2022 and Olympic MVP), Cycling (Peter Sagan - legendary 'Tourminator', record 7-time Green Jersey winner at the Tour de France and triple consecutive World Champion), Slalom Canoeing (undisputed Olympic superpower: Michal Martikán - 5 Olympic medals, Pavol and Peter Hochschorner - triple Olympic Gold, Elena Kaliská), Football (Marek Hamšík, Milan Škriniar, Stanislav Lobotka - reached knockout stages at UEFA Euro 2016, 2024), Alpine Skiing (Petra Vlhová - Olympic Slalom Gold medalist Beijing 2022 and World Cup Overall Champion).
media: RTVS / STVR (Slovenská televízia a rozhlas - public broadcaster: Jednotka, Dvojka, :24 news channel), TV Markíza (leading commercial network), TV JOJ, TA3 (24-hour news channel), Denník N, SME, Pravda, Hospodárske noviny, TASR news agency.
clothing: Traditional Kroj (magnificent regional folk costumes featuring heavily embroidered puff sleeves, pleated lace ruffs, colorful silk aprons, floral headpieces / parta, and men's broad brass-buckled leather belts); modern European street fashion and alpine outdoor clothing.
holidays: Day of the Establishment of the Slovak Republic (January 1)
Day of Saints Cyril and Methodius (July 5)
Slovak National Uprising Day (August 29 - celebrations in Banská Bystrica)
Day of the Constitution of the Slovak Republic (September 1)

Christmas Eve (Štedrý deň - December 24) and Christmas (December 25-26)

travelNotes: Hike around the crystal-clear alpine waters of Štrbské Pleso beneath the jagged granite spires of the High Tatras; explore the monumental medieval stone ramparts of Spiš Castle rising above the surrounding valleys; photograph the white painted gingerbread-style timber houses of Čičmany; ride the high-speed elevator to the flying-saucer UFO restaurant overlooking the Danube in Bratislava; savor a piping hot wooden bowl of bryndzové halušky topped with sizzling bacon cubes and accompanied by a cold glass of Kofola.
shortSummary: Slovakia is a captivating Central European mountain jewel where the soaring alpine peaks of the High Tatras and over 180 dramatic castles meet the fairy-tale painted village of Čičmany, world-record car manufacturing prowess per capita, delicious bryndzové halušky, and 100% clean nuclear energy.
geography: Spanning 49,036 km² across Central Europe. Highest point: Gerlachovský štít (2,655 m in the High Tatras - highest peak in the Carpathian Mountains); lowest point: Bodrog River (94 m). Longest river: Váh River (406 km entirely in Slovakia) and Danube River (172 km bordering in the southwest). Climate: Temperate continental climate with warm summers and cold, snowy winters; significant alpine conditions across the High and Low Tatras with ski seasons lasting into late spring.
economy: Economy with GDP nominal of $140 billion (approx. 2026) ($25,800 (over $45,000 PPP) per capita). Leading sectors: Services 61%, Industry 36%, Agriculture 3%. Main industries: Automotive manufacturing (undisputed world champion in cars produced per capita: over 1 million vehicles produced annually across four major auto plants: Volkswagen Slovakia in Bratislava, Stellantis in Trnava, Kia Motors in Žilina, Jaguar Land Rover in Nitra, plus the new Volvo Cars all-electric megasite in Košice), Information technology and cybersecurity (ESET - global cybersecurity titan and maker of NOD32 antivirus; Pixel Federation - game software), Electrical engineering and consumer electronics (Samsung Electronics, Foxconn), Metallurgy and steel production (U.S. Steel Košice - major blast furnace steel complex), Machinery, industrial robotics, and defense equipment (ZVS Holding, Konstrukta Defence - Zuzana howitzers), Chemicals, plastics, and pharmaceutical manufacturing (Slovnaft oil refinery, Duslo Šaľa). Key exports: Motor vehicles, SUVs, and automotive components (representing over 45% of total merchandise exports), Electrical machinery, televisions, and electronic equipment, Iron, steel, and flat-rolled metal products, Industrial machinery and nuclear equipment, Rubber tires and automotive parts, Plastics, chemicals, and refined fuels.
culture: Rich cultural traditions featuring cuisine (Bryndzové Halušky (the beloved national dish: small soft potato dumplings / gnocchi tossed with creamy, tangy unpasteurized sheep milk Bryndza cheese, smothered in crispy golden smoked bacon cubes / škvarky, and drizzled with hot bacon drippings, traditionally washed down with a glass of sour sheep milk / žinčica), Bryndzové Pirohy (crescent-shaped potato dough pockets stuffed with bryndza and mashed potatoes, topped with bacon and sour cream), Kapustnica (rich, comforting Christmas and winter soup made from fermented sauerkraut, smoked pork sausages, smoked ham, dried forest porcini mushrooms, and prunes), Vyprážaný syr (crispy breaded fried cheese served with French fries and tartar sauce), Zemiakové placky (crispy garlic and marjoram potato pancakes), Gulášová polievka (hearty goulash soup cooked in an outdoor cauldron / kotlík), Skalický trdelník (spit-roasted sweet walnut pastry roll with PDO/PGI European status), Bratislavské rožky (crescent rolls filled with sweet poppy seeds or crushed walnuts), and iconic drinks: Kofola (beloved Czechoslovak herbal cola with 14 natural fruit and herbal ingredients, created in 1960), Tatratea (legendary herbal tea liqueur from the High Tatras, with strengths from 22% to 72%), Borovička (juniper berry spirit), and crisp Slovak lager beers (Zlatý Bažant / Golden Pheasant, Šariš).), traditional music and dance (The Fujara (monumental, deep-toned, over-2-meter-long traditional wooden overtone bass flute played by shepherds, declared by UNESCO as a Masterpiece of Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity in 2005); classical composer Eugen Suchoň (Krútňava - national opera), Ján Cikker; Slovak Philharmonic Orchestra; pop/rock icons (Elán, Miroslav Žbirka, Richard Müller, IMT Smile, Horkýže Slíže).; Traditional folk dances: Odzemok (acrobatic shepherd axe dance with shepherds' hatchets / valaška), Karička (whirlwind female circle dance of eastern Slovakia), Čardáš (passionate couple dance with dizzying spins); modern contemporary dance company Divadlo Štúdio tanca in Banská Bystrica.), literature (Pavol Országh Hviezdoslav (National Poet: The Forester's Wife / Hájnikova žena, Bloody Sonnets), Ľudovít Štúr, Martin Kukučín, Jozef Cíger-Hronský, Ladislav Mňačko (The Taste of Power), contemporary authors: Pavel Vilikovský, Daniela Capitáňová.), and sports (Ice hockey (undisputed national religion: 2002 IIHF World Champions, historic Olympic Bronze medal at Beijing 2022; NHL legends Peter Šťastný, Stan Mikita, Marián Hossa - Hall of Famer, Marián Gáborík, Zdeno Chára - tallest player in NHL history, Juraj Slafkovský - #1 overall NHL draft pick 2022 and Olympic MVP), Cycling (Peter Sagan - legendary 'Tourminator', record 7-time Green Jersey winner at the Tour de France and triple consecutive World Champion), Slalom Canoeing (undisputed Olympic superpower: Michal Martikán - 5 Olympic medals, Pavol and Peter Hochschorner - triple Olympic Gold, Elena Kaliská), Football (Marek Hamšík, Milan Škriniar, Stanislav Lobotka - reached knockout stages at UEFA Euro 2016, 2024), Alpine Skiing (Petra Vlhová - Olympic Slalom Gold medalist Beijing 2022 and World Cup Overall Champion).).

name: Slovenia
nationalDay: June 25 (Statehood Day - declaration of independence in 1991) and February 8 (Prešeren Day - Slovenian Cultural Holiday)

motto: None (informal: I Feel SLOVEnia)

Lake Bled (famed picture-postcard alpine lake with a teardrop island and cliff castle)

climate: Sub-Mediterranean along the Adriatic coast with hot summers and mild winters; continental in the central and eastern plains; alpine in the northwestern mountain ranges with heavy snowfall and pristine ski slopes

Winter avalanches in the Julian Alps

Marine conservation along the compact Adriatic coastline
Forest resilience against bark beetle and extreme storm damage
biodiversity: Europe's greenest and most biologically diverse haven: over 60% of the territory is covered in lush forests (third most forested country in Europe after Finland and Sweden); home to over 1,000 wild brown bears (one of Europe's densest populations), grey wolves, Eurasian lynx, golden eagles, and the enigmatic olm / 'human fish' (Proteus anguinus - blind cave salamander living up to 100 years in the subterranean karst caves of Postojna and Škocjan)
languages: Slovene (official South Slavic language, which famously preserves the archaic dual grammatical grammatical number)
Italian (co-official in coastal municipalities)
Hungarian (co-official in Prekmurje)
currency: Euro (EUR, € - adopted January 1, 2007; first of the 2004 EU accession states to adopt the Euro)
headOfState: President Nataša Pirc Musar (first female President of Slovenia)
legislature: Parliament of Slovenia (National Assembly / Državni zbor of 90 seats and National Council / Državni svet of 40 seats)
mainPoliticalParties: Freedom Movement (Gibanje Svoboda, led by Robert Golob)
latestElections: Parliamentary election April 2022; presidential election November 2022; European Parliament election June 2024; next parliamentary election 2026
politicalSituation: Progressive, green-oriented social democracy; elected as a non-permanent member of the United Nations Security Council for the 2024–2025 term; pioneer of circular green economy policies; formally recognized the State of Palestine in June 2024.
foreignRelations: Member of European Union (joined 2004), Eurozone (joined 2007), Schengen Area (joined 2007), NATO (joined 2004), OECD, and WTO; elected member of the United Nations Security Council for 2024–2025, actively championing international humanitarian law, environmental protection, and mediation.
military: Slovenian Armed Forces (Slovenska vojska: Land Forces, Air Force, and Naval Division with patrol boats Triglav and Ankaran; professional force participating in NATO, EU, and UN peacekeeping missions).
adminDivisions: 212 local municipalities (občine), of which 12 have urban city status, grouped into 12 statistical regions
history: Settled by Slavs in the 6th century, establishing the early medieval Slavic principality of Carantania (Karantanija), famous for the democratic ritual of the Installation of the Dukes on the Prince's Stone. Absorbed into the Frankish Empire and subsequently ruled for centuries as Austrian hereditary crown lands under the Habsburg Monarchy (Carniola, Styria, Carinthia, and the Gorizia-Gradisca littoral). Primož Trubar published the first printed books in Slovene (Catechismus and Abecedarium) in 1550 during the Protestant Reformation. Jurij Dalmatin translated the complete Bible into Slovene in 1584. Following WWI and the dissolution of Austria-Hungary, Slovenes joined the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes in 1918 (later Yugoslavia). Heroically resisted Nazi and Fascist occupation in WWII through the partisan resistance movement. Re-emerged as the most prosperous and industrialized constituent republic of socialist Yugoslavia. In December 1990, an overwhelming 88.5% voted for independence in a national referendum. Proclaimed independence on June 25, 1991, successfully defending its sovereignty in the brief Ten-Day War. Transformed rapidly into an advanced high-income knowledge economy, becoming the first post-communist country to adopt the Euro in 2007.
recentEvents2020_2026: Served on the United Nations Security Council as an elected non-permanent member for the 2024–2025 term; held the rotating Presidency of the UN Security Council in September 2024, leading high-level debates on international peace and multilateralism; formally recognized the State of Palestine in June 2024; advanced the landmark JEK2 project for a second 1,200 MW nuclear reactor at the Krško Nuclear Power Plant; Nova Gorica prepared to shine as the European Capital of Culture 2025 (jointly with Gorizia, Italy); celebrated historic sporting triumphs with Tadej Pogačar winning the Giro d'Italia, Tour de France, and World Road Championship 'Triple Crown' in 2024.

Primož Trubar (Protestant reformer who printed the first Slovene books in 1550)
Jože Plečnik (visionary modernist architect who transformed Ljubljana, Prague Castle, and Vienna)
